name: Everyone
label: Hand off a task of any size.

cards.title: Action tracking
cards.headline: Keep up with meetings all day
cards.body: Horizon reads each transcript, pulls action items and owners into one list, posts it for the team in Slack, and follows up on opens before the next meeting on Google Calendar.
cards.prompt: After each of my meetings this week, read the transcript and pull out action items and owners. Post a running list to my team channel and remind owners two days before the next meeting if their item’s still open.

cards.title: Feedback digest
cards.headline: Organize customer feedback into a digest
cards.body: Horizon pulls feedback from Slack, Gmail, support, and survey tools, clusters it by theme, ties it to the roadmap, and delivers a weekly digest in Word everyone can review.
cards.prompt: Pull customer feedback from Slack, email, and support from the last week. Group it into themes with counts, tie each to a roadmap item, and post the digest to my team channel.

cards.title: Budget reforecast
cards.headline: Update your H2 budget for your leadership check-in
cards.body: Keep your budget up to date. Work with Horizon to roll H2 numbers forward with a new headcount plan in Horizon for Excel, and it flags every changed cell with notes.
cards.prompt: Take my H1 budget model and roll it forward through H2 using this new headcount plan. Flag every cell you change and note anywhere it doesn’t tie out to the original.

name: Marketing
label: Share an idea, get a draft back.

cards.title: Campaign readout
cards.headline: See what moved and why before your day starts
cards.body: Set it up once. Every Monday, Horizon pulls last week’s web, ad, and channel numbers from Amplitude and BigQuery, flags anything over 10%, and delivers it to you as a PowerPoint deck.
cards.prompt: Every Monday, pull last week’s web, ad, and channel numbers from Amplitude and BigQuery, compare to the week before, flag anything that moved more than 10%, and put it in a deck I can review before it goes out.

cards.title: Asset creation
cards.headline: Build on-brand assets to show the team
cards.body: Build on-brand social assets, decks, or landing page mockups quickly. Upload your brand guidelines or writing skill, say what you need, and Horizon starts designing.
cards.prompt: Build a social set for the Fall Readout using our brand guidelines. Three 4:5 posts — a stat, a headline, and a trend — as one proof sheet.

cards.title: Audience intelligence
cards.headline: What your audience is saying before the next meeting
cards.body: Horizon gathers feedback from your Gmail survey label and #brand-mentions in Slack, plus social chatter and news, then clusters it into themes for a prioritized readout.
cards.prompt: Pull feedback from my Gmail survey label and the #brand-mentions channel in Slack, along with recent social chatter and news coverage. Cluster it into themes and give me a prioritized readout of what needs attention this week.

cards.title: Call prep
cards.headline: Prep for every call before your meeting
cards.body: Stay on top of your meetings. Horizon reads today’s schedule in Google Calendar, pulls the relevant threads from Salesforce and Slack, and hands you a short brief in Word before each one.
cards.prompt: Look at today’s calendar and pull recent Slack mentions for each external meeting. Give me a short brief per meeting: who I’m meeting, recent context from Salesforce, and what to bring up.

cards.title: QBR deck
cards.headline: Assemble your QBR for review
cards.body: Get ahead of your deck. Horizon pulls the account from Salesforce, plus last quarter’s deck and notes from Google Drive, asks what it needs, then builds on your PowerPoint template.
cards.prompt: Pull the Northfield record from Salesforce, last quarter’s QBR deck, and my notes from this folder. Ask me anything you need, then build the new QBR on our template.

cards.title: CRM hygiene
cards.headline: Keep opportunities up to date before you sign off
cards.body: Hand off the upkeep. Horizon reads your call transcripts and notes, drafts the opportunity field updates in Word, then fills them in Salesforce and flags and fixes data-quality issues with your approval.
cards.prompt: Read my last week of call transcripts and notes, then update the matching Salesforce opportunities: next steps, notes, methodology, and competition. Show me the changes before saving.

cards.title: Earnings comps
cards.headline: Build a comps table ahead of a meeting in minutes
cards.body: Horizon pulls the transcript and filing, extracts guidance and KPIs, compares to consensus, and hands you a PowerPoint slide with the comps table in Excel behind it.
cards.prompt: Pull the latest earnings transcript and 10-Q for Dunhollow. Extract guidance, key KPIs, and commentary, compare to last quarter, and build a comps table against these peers.

cards.title: Month-end close
cards.headline: Reconcile every region in one summary before lunch
cards.body: Keep your data clean. Ask Horizon to reconcile regional exports, each in their own format, into one consolidated summary in Horizon for Excel with variances flagged for review.
cards.prompt: Here are this month’s regional actuals exports. Reconcile them into one summary, flag any variances against budget, and note anything that doesn’t tie out.

cards.title: Budget reforecast
cards.headline: Update your H2 budget for your leadership check-in
cards.body: Keep your budget up to date. Work with Horizon to roll H2 numbers forward with a new headcount plan in Horizon for Excel, and it flags every changed cell with notes.
cards.prompt: Take my H1 budget model and roll it forward through H2 using this new headcount plan. Flag every cell you change and note anywhere it doesn’t tie out to the original.

cards.title: JD check
cards.headline: Catch an issue before you post a job description
cards.body: Ask Horizon to review a job description before it goes out. It checks it against your leveling guide for your review, then returns the edited doc in Word and an interview kit.
cards.prompt: Check this job description against our leveling guide. Give me back an edited version and an interview kit.

cards.title: Survey readout
cards.headline: Cluster comments into themes before the meeting
cards.body: Hand Horizon your open-text survey results and ask it to group them by theme and start your executive deck. It works in your PowerPoint presentation. You edit and make it yours.
cards.prompt: Here’s our engagement survey export. Theme the open-text responses, quantify how often each theme comes up, and build the exec readout deck on our template.

cards.title: Merit analysis
cards.headline: Do merit math and draft comp letters before you go
cards.body: Make compensation packets easier. Run the merit analysis in Horizon for Excel, then Horizon picks the context back up to draft the comp letters in Horizon for Word.
cards.prompt: Run the merit analysis on this comp data against the budget, then generate a comp letter for each employee from the template.

cards.title: Legal research drafting
cards.headline: Draft legal research and memos to prep the day
cards.body: Start your morning with the research already done. Ask Horizon to pull case law from CourtListener, verify citations, and draft a memo in Word summarizing the precedent.
cards.prompt: Research case law on this issue in our jurisdiction. Verify citations against CourtListener, summarize the controlling precedent, and draft a memo on how it applies to our matter.

cards.title: Deposition prep
cards.headline: Prepare for depositions and witness interviews
cards.body: Walk in with a working list, not a script. Ask Horizon to pull the documents from Everlaw, build a chronology, and lay out your questions by topic in an Excel spreadsheet.
cards.prompt: Pull every document tagged to the witness in Everlaw, build a chronology of key events, and put deposition questions in a spreadsheet, organized by topic, one row per question, with the supporting document cited and a column to mark each one covered.

cards.title: Contract redline
cards.headline: Redline NDAs or SOWs before the end of the day
cards.body: Speed up contract review with services like Ironclad and iManage. Ask Horizon to redline a contract against your playbook in Word and get back tracked changes for review.
cards.prompt: Counterparty marked up our SOW. Review their changes against our playbook, flag deviations, and output as a doc.

cards.title: Action tracking
cards.headline: Keep up with meetings all day
cards.body: Horizon reads each transcript, pulls action items and owners into one list, posts it for the team in Slack, and follows up on opens before the next meeting on Google Calendar.
cards.prompt: After each of my meetings this week, read the transcript and pull out action items and owners. Post a running list to my team channel and remind owners two days before the next meeting if their item’s still open.

cards.title: Feedback digest
cards.headline: Organize customer feedback into a digest
cards.body: Horizon pulls feedback from Slack, Gmail, support, and survey tools, clusters it by theme, ties it to the roadmap, and delivers a weekly digest in Word everyone can review.
cards.prompt: Pull customer feedback from Slack, email, and support from the last week. Group it into themes with counts, tie each to a roadmap item, and post the digest to my team channel.

cards.title: Metrics dashboard
cards.headline: Understand your product data before you sign off
cards.body: Horizon connects to analytics services like BigQuery, or reviews an export from Google Sheets, and builds a metrics dashboard that answers your data questions with charts.
cards.prompt: Connect to my analytics data and build a product metrics dashboard: DAU/WAU, weekly retention, funnel conversion, and feature adoption. Explain any trends I should pay attention to this week.
